hooks.text: A billion-light-year hole in space could be a scar from another universe.
Astronomers found a void spanning up to two billion light-years.
There is a massive region of space containing almost no matter at all.

title: The Billion-Light-Year Void in Eridanus
description: Astronomers discovered an immense cosmic wasteland in the constellation Eridanus that defies standard cosmological models.

beats.text: A billion-light-year hole in space could be a scar from another universe.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a multiverse bubble collision, 2015

beats.text: In 2004, astronomers scanning the cosmic background radiation discovered an unexpected anomaly.
beats.visual: NASA WMAP cosmic microwave background radiation map, 2003

beats.text: This massive Cold Spot in the constellation Eridanus is seventy microkelvin cooler than average.
beats.visual: Eridanus constellation star chart and borders

beats.text: The anomaly spans up to two billion light-years and is largely devoid of stars and gas.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the cosmic web and voids
queries: large scale structure of the cosmos

beats.text: As ancient photons cross this vacuum, the universe's expansion stretches the region, causing light to lose energy.
beats.visual: Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect photon energy loss diagram

beats.text: The European Space Agency's Planck satellite confirmed this bizarre emptiness in 2013.
beats.visual: ESA Planck spacecraft artist illustration in deep space

beats.text: Some researchers theorize the Cold Spot is an imprint of a collision with a parallel universe.
beats.visual: Multiverse bubble collision artist concept illustration

beats.text: That cosmic bruise remains carved across the sky by a parallel universe.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a multiverse bubble collision, 2015

better_than_last: This episode applies the proven mystery structure with a sharp contradiction hook and a seamless loop that flows directly back into the opening claim.
